name: Sleater-Kinney
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Named for a freeway exit outside Olympia, two guitars and no bass, a breakup sung out loud on record, a breakdown in Brussels, and a comeback nobody knew they'd already recorded.

eras.title: Two guitars, no bass, one exit off I-5
eras.text: Corin Tucker of Heavens to Betsy and Carrie Brownstein of Excuse 17 started Sleater-Kinney in Olympia as a side project. Two records in two years on the queercore label Chainsaw Records made them critics' favorites before they had a steady drummer.

years.h: Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein start a side project in Olympia
years.p: Tucker has just graduated from The Evergreen State College, where Brownstein is still a student. They name the band after Sleater Kinney Road in Lacey, the I-5 exit 108 turnoff.
years.xp: The road itself is named for two 19th-century families, the Sleaters and Henry and Martha Kinney, who lived in Olympia's South Bay neighborhood.

years.h: Recording the debut on the last night of a trip to Australia
years.p: On their final night in Australia, Tucker and Brownstein, a couple at the time, record the songs that become their first album.

years.h: Sleater-Kinney, the debut on Chainsaw
years.p: The Australian recordings come out as Sleater-Kinney's first album on Chainsaw Records, with [[Lora MacFarlane|15ab5023-3b1c-4bdf-afe5-184932a6edfb]] behind the kit.

years.h: Call the Doctor: written in three weeks, recorded in four days
years.p: Produced by [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]] for Chainsaw, the album ranks third in the Village Voice's 1996 critics' poll. It sold 6,000 copies by March 1997 and 60,000 in the US by 2015.
years.xp:
There's no bass player. Tucker said two guitars gave them freedom to write lines that go back and forth. She wrote out of frustration with work and with how society makes people consumerized and commodified.

AllMusic called it pure, undiluted punk. Rolling Stone later put it at No. 49 among the greatest albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Spin outs Carrie Brownstein at 21
years.p: Spin magazine reports that Brownstein is bisexual and that she had been in a relationship with bandmate Corin Tucker. Brownstein later described herself more broadly as queer.

years.h: Lora MacFarlane's Australian visa runs out
years.p: Drummer Lora MacFarlane leaves soon after Call the Doctor comes out, when her visa expires. Misty Farrell and Toni Gogin also drum for the band in its early years.

eras.title: Janet Weiss completes the band
eras.text: Janet Weiss of Quasi came to a show, joined, and gave the band a drummer who knew the Stones and Lightnin' Hopkins as well as punk. Sleater-Kinney moved to Kill Rock Stars, dug out of a Seattle snowstorm, and made the record that took them worldwide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Janet Weiss · Wikipedia: Dig Me Out · Wikipedia: Quasi
years.h: Janet Weiss joins after seeing Sleater-Kinney play
years.p: Weiss, drummer in Portland's [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]], becomes the band's fourth drummer after watching one of their shows. She stays for ten years, then five more.
years.xp:
Weiss started drumming in The Furies at 22 after one lesson and two weeks of practice. She moved to Portland in 1989 and formed Quasi with Sam Coomes, her former husband, in 1993.

Tucker told Addicted to Noise that Weiss became the bottom end and the solidness the band had always wanted.

years.h: Dig Me Out, named for a Seattle snowstorm
years.p: Recorded in eight days at John and Stu's Place in Seattle over winter 1996–97, when the band had to dig the studio out of the snow. Kill Rock Stars releases it. It's No. 4 in the Pazz & Jop poll.
years.xp:
Producer [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]] noted that Call the Doctor took four days; the new label paid for twice that. Robert Christgau wrote that the band was so confident of its ability to please that it couldn't stop.

Rolling Stone ranked it No. 189 on its 2020 list of the greatest albums of all time.

years.h: One More Hour: the breakup, sung by both of them
years.p: On Dig Me Out, the song One More Hour is about the end of Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein's romantic relationship. They sing it together.

years.h: The Hot Rock reaches for a bigger audience
years.p: The first of three albums Wikipedia describes as pushing Sleater-Kinney toward the mainstream.

years.h: Corin Tucker marries filmmaker Lance Bangs in Iceland
years.p: Tucker and director Lance Bangs marry in Iceland. They go on to have two children.

years.h: All Hands on the Bad One
years.p: Sleater-Kinney's fifth album keeps building the audience while staying on Kill Rock Stars.

eras.title: America's best rock band
eras.text: Critics started using superlatives, Pearl Jam took them into arenas, and the band answered with the loudest record it ever made, on a new label with a new producer.

years.h: Greil Marcus names them America's best rock band
years.p: The critic Greil Marcus gives Sleater-Kinney the title in 2001. Robert Christgau calls them one of the essential rock groups of the early 2000s.

years.h: One Beat, the last Kill Rock Stars album
years.p: Sleater-Kinney's sixth album completes its push toward bigger rooms.

years.h: Opening arenas for Pearl Jam
years.p: Sleater-Kinney supports [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] at many North American arena shows. The band later credits the experience with inspiring its next album.

years.h: The Woods: Sub Pop, Dave Fridmann and an 11-minute song
years.p: Recorded mostly live at Tarbox Road Studios in Cassadaga, New York with [[Dave Fridmann|6b09687f-72de-4337-9a0b-da8f6248ce7c]]. It's Sleater-Kinney's first album on Sub Pop and its heaviest.
years.xp:
Let's Call It Love (11:01) and Night Light were cut as a single 15-minute take after Carrie Brownstein noticed they were in the same key. Only vocals and a few guitars were overdubbed.

It reached No. 80 on the Billboard 200 and sold 94,000 US copies by 2015. Q gave it two stars; Rolling Stone later put it at No. 72 of the decade.

eras.title: The breakdown in Brussels
eras.text: Sleater-Kinney ended at a peak, and it wasn't planned. Brownstein told the whole story nine years later in her memoir.

years.big: Two days of shingles, ten years of band
years.h: Carrie Brownstein breaks down in Brussels and ends the band
years.p: Two days before a European tour, Brownstein gets shingles and is kept apart from Janet Weiss, who never had chickenpox. Before the show at Le Botanique in Brussels, she breaks down in front of Tucker and Weiss.
years.xp:
Brownstein says the shingles came from anxiety, and being isolated from her bandmates made her mental health worse. Corin Tucker was also exhausted by touring and wanted time with her family.

Brownstein told the story in her 2015 memoir Hunger Makes Me a Modern Girl.

years.h: Indefinite hiatus: no plans for tours or recordings
years.p: Sleater-Kinney announces the break. The band plays Lollapalooza, its last major public show.

years.h: The last show, at Portland's Crystal Ballroom
years.p: Sleater-Kinney's final concert before the hiatus is at the Crystal Ballroom in Portland, Oregon.

eras.title: Portlandia, Wild Flag and the Jicks
eras.text: With the band on ice, all three members stayed busy. Weiss drummed for Stephen Malkmus, Tucker went solo, and Brownstein started a new band and a TV show that made her famous far outside music.

years.h: Janet Weiss drums for Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks
years.p: Weiss plays on [[Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks|98e4bf9e-9e33-4f07-9962-f7c1c2d773ba]]' Real Emotional Trash (2008) and Mirror Traffic (2011), leaving before the second album's tour.

years.h: Corin Tucker's solo debut, 1,000 Years
years.p: Released on Kill Rock Stars with Unwound's Sara Lund and Seth Lorinczi of [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]]. Kill My Blues follows in 2012.

years.h: Portlandia premieres on IFC
years.p: Carrie Brownstein and Fred Armisen's sketch show runs until 2018 and wins Emmy and Peabody awards.

years.h: Wild Flag: Brownstein and Weiss with Mary Timony
years.p: [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]], with [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] of [[Helium|573510d6-bb5d-4d07-b0aa-ea6afe39e28d]] and Rebecca Cole of the Minders, releases its only album on Merge Records. By 2014 the band is done.

eras.title: The secret record
eras.text: Sleater-Kinney recorded a comeback album before telling anyone, then made its biggest-charting record and lost the drummer who had defined it.

years.h: Sleater-Kinney announces No Cities to Love, already made
years.p: The band had recorded in secret, mostly at Tiny Telephone in San Francisco with [[John Goodmanson|6f62dbe4-701c-4c4b-a204-420996982e9f]]. The Start Together vinyl box set comes out the same year.

years.h: Sub Pop streams the comeback album three weeks early by accident
years.p: The label's slip puts No Cities to Love online weeks before release.

years.src: Wikipedia: No Cities to Love · Wikipedia: Sleater-Kinney
years.h: No Cities to Love reaches No. 18
years.p: Sub Pop releases the comeback album to near-universal praise. The New York Times' Jon Pareles calls it the first great album of 2015. Stereogum's Tom Breihan calls them the greatest rock band of the past two decades.
years.xp: The title track's video features Andy Samberg, Sarah Silverman, Brie Larson and Gerard Way. The March 20 show at La Cigale in Paris became the band's first live album, Live in Paris, in January 2017.

years.h: Carrie Brownstein's memoir, Hunger Makes Me a Modern Girl
years.p: Brownstein's book tells the band's story, including the 2006 breakdown that ended its first run.

years.h: St. Vincent will produce the next album
years.p: Sleater-Kinney announces that [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]], Annie Clark, is producing its ninth album, recorded in Portland.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Center Won't Hold · Wikipedia: Janet Weiss
years.h: Janet Weiss quits a month before The Center Won't Hold
years.p: Weiss announces on Twitter that it's time for her to move on. She said Tucker and Brownstein had made clear she would no longer be a creative equal, only the drummer.
years.xp: Weiss said the roles within the band had changed and she didn't want to play songs live she hadn't helped create. She had been in the band since 1996 and played on every album from Dig Me Out on.

years.h: The Center Won't Hold, produced by St. Vincent
years.p: The St. Vincent-produced album comes out on Mom + Pop and reaches No. 27 on the Billboard 200, No. 2 on the alternative chart.

years.h: First show without Janet Weiss, at Hopscotch
years.p: Sleater-Kinney plays North Carolina's Hopscotch Music Festival with new drummer Angie Boylan.

eras.title: Two of them, and a loss
eras.text: Down to the founding pair, Sleater-Kinney kept making records fast. Then a family tragedy reshaped the next one.

years.h: Path of Wellness, the first album as a duo
years.p: Led by the single Worry With You, released May 11. That summer the band tours with [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]].

years.h: Carrie Brownstein's mother and stepfather die in a car accident
years.p: Brownstein's mother and stepfather are killed in a car crash in Italy. Half of the next album was written before, half after.

years.h: Little Rope, made with grief in the room
years.p: Produced by [[John Congleton|6da4067f-e6ce-49b6-925c-56e017075038]] in Portland and released on Loma Vista. Pitchfork called it the band's sturdiest rock record since No Cities to Love.
